title: BOOM TOWN — Highlight Reel
summary: “This is not utopia. This is a neighborhood of speculation. This is Times Square. Or that fracking town in North Dakota with the $15 Budweisers while supplies last.” - Peter Burr Peter Burr’s BOOM TOWN is a fictional blockchain neighborhood inspired by the boom and bust cycles of speculation, echoing the make-shift settlements of the American West that rose and fell with resource discoveries. These historical boomtowns, animated by Manifest Destiny and get-rich-quick schemes, attracted prospectors and speculators, often becoming ghost towns once resources depleted, though some, like San Francisco, reinvented themselves. Like most of Burr’s works, BOOM TOWN is a richly crafted narrative world, evocative yet mysterious. Displaying a gift for images that hover between abstraction and figuration, they invite viewer interpretation. Inspired by video games, Burr’s compositions draw on generative dynamics and rule-based systems. Each of the eight works follows a precise logic for generating its architecture, ground, shadows, and colors, reminiscent of 8-bit video games, early computer graphics, and CAD drawings. Burr has long been fascinated by architecture and utopian built environments, exploring the tension between idealistic design and unpredictable lived reality. Online, architectural metaphors often describe information systems or digital real estate. Importantly, BOOM TOWN’s locations are devoid of people—empty streets, vacant windows. Burr highlights this vacancy and potentiality as sites of projection, speculation, and collective imagination. On day one, BOOM TOWN is empty structures; through collecting, it becomes populated by its NFT proprietors. At a time when web3 is largely a vacant space, Burr underscores that *we* will determine its social and civic life, populating and activating these spaces, and choosing to build them differently.
